shorts.title: Platner Quit The Race, Then Paid His Wife $20,246 In Severance #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Folks, Graham Platner dropped out of Maine's Senate race on July 8. [deadpan] Quitting, apparently, is not the same as stopping spending. His campaign has spent about two point three million dollars since July, per the Washington Examiner's read of his new FEC filing. His wife's severance check? Twenty thousand, two hundred forty-six dollars, the biggest the campaign issued. And Troy Jackson, the Democrat who replaced him? [beat] [sarcastic] Zero. Not a dime to Jackson, not a dime to the Maine Democratic Party. [beat] That's not a campaign, friends, that's a going-out-of-business sale with a Senate logo. Matthew six, twenty-one: 'For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.' [beat] [mischievously] And the treasure, it seems, didn't go to the party. Democrats, is this what you call team spirit? [warm] Subscribe, we roast the news every day.

claims.text: Graham Platner dropped out of Maine's Senate race on July 8 and his campaign has spent about $2.3 million since July, per a new FEC filing.
The campaign paid his wife, Amy Gertner, $20,246 in severance, described as the largest severance check the campaign issued.
The campaign made no contributions to Troy Jackson, the Democrat who replaced Platner, or to the Maine Democratic Party.

shorts.title: Newsom In New Hampshire: Israel Aid "Has To Be Conditioned" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Folks, California's Gavin Newsom flew to Manchester, New Hampshire this weekend. Strange, since nobody's running for president. [deadpan] The Washington Examiner says he's test-driving a 2028 run, and his first big policy stop? Israel. [beat] He told the paper, quote, 'Aid has to be conditioned.' And he says that's quickly becoming the Democratic Party's consensus position. [sarcastic] Funny how consensus always shows up right where the primary voters are. [beat] Genesis twelve, three: 'I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee.' [beat] [mischievously] Gavin, that verse didn't come with a polling average. America's closest Middle East ally, and a California governor wants strings. Democrats, is that your party's new foreign policy? Tell me in the comments. [warm] Subscribe, we roast the news every day.

claims.text: Gavin Newsom told the Washington Examiner on Saturday that military aid to Israel 'has to be conditioned,' speaking in Manchester, New Hampshire.
The Washington Examiner says Newsom is test-driving a 2028 run for president on the New Hampshire trip.
Newsom said the view is quickly becoming the Democratic Party's consensus position.

shorts.title: Trump Once Called Stephen A. Smith "Dumb As A Rock." Then Came Dinner #Shorts
shorts.hook: "Dumb As A Rock"... Then A 4-Hour Dinner
shorts.narration: [amused] Folks, earlier this year Donald Trump called Stephen A. Smith an 'arrogant fool' and 'dumb as a rock.' [beat] Thursday night? Four hours at the White House dinner table, with Bill Maher. [deadpan] Smith says Trump 'answered every single question,' and quote, 'He wouldn't let us leave.' [beat] [sarcastic] That's either hospitality or a hostage situation, and Stephen A. says he liked it. Trump called him 'great.' Smith, a registered independent, said it was a 'very substantive evening.' Proverbs fifteen, one: 'A soft answer turneth away wrath.' [beat] Turns out all it takes to turn off the Trump Derangement is a good dinner and a ballroom tour. [mischievously] Democrats, if Maher and Stephen A. both come home impressed, what exactly is your party afraid of? [warm] Subscribe, we roast the news every day.

claims.text: Stephen A. Smith said he had a four-hour dinner with Bill Maher and President Trump at the White House on Thursday night, saying 'We were there for over four hours in the White House.'
Smith said Trump 'answered every single question' and 'He wouldn't let us leave.' He called it 'a very substantive evening.'
Earlier this year Trump had attacked Smith, calling him an 'arrogant fool' and 'dumb as a rock'; after the dinner Trump said 'Stephen A. is great.'
Smith said 'I'm a registered independent' and Trump said the group 'even took a little tour of the ballroom.'

slides.label: A soft answer turneth away wrath. (Proverbs 15:1)
